title: NFL Card Watch: The Seahawks and Patriots Run It Back to Kick Off the 2026 Season
summary: The biggest Patriots and Seahawks cards heading into kickoff.
body_markdown:
If you listen closely, you can hear it: the clash of pads, the ref’s whistle, and, the jingle of theme songs from CBS, Fox, NBC, ESPN, Amazon Prim, and, newly, Netflix. Yes, my friends, the rumors are true: football is officially *back* !


The 2026 NFL season kicks off tonight at 8:20 p.m. Eastern when the Seattle Seahawks host the New England Patriots at Lumen Field on NBC—the first season opener on a Wednesday since the New York Giants hosted the Dallas Cowboys in 2012. Why are we kicking off on what is traditionally a non-football day, you ask? Because the NFL is sending the San Francisco 49ers and the Los Angeles Rams to Melbourne, Australia for a special Thursday night game that marks the NFL’s first regular season game Down Under.


Tonight’s matchup isn’t just the kick off to a new season, it’s a highly-anticipated rematch of Super Bowl LX, when the Seahawks beat the Patriots 29-13 back in February. Neither team looks exactly the same as they did seven months ago, but that’s what makes Week 1 so special: new beginnings.


Let’s go!


## **Running It Back:**


The last time these two teams squared off,[Kenneth Walker III](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Kenneth%20Walker%20III&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ran through, over, and around New England’s defense on his way to winning Super Bowl LX MVP. While star quarterback[Sam Darnold](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Sam%20Darnold&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) is still calling plays for Seattle, his running mate now calls Arrowhead home. When your wide receiver room features[Jaxon Smith-Njigba](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Jaxon%20Smith-Njigba&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ,[Cooper Kupp](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Cooper%20Kupp&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , and Rashid Shaheed, along with tight end[AJ Barner](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=AJ%20Barner&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , it’s tough to wallow.
‍
New England, meanwhile, not only arrives with something to prove, but with a similar roster. While there are some holes to fill, their young quarterback,[Drake Maye](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Drake%20Maye&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , is looking to build on a strong 2025 regular season where he led the league in passer rating. (Let’s not talk about his postseason…) Can he top his breakout year—especially with a tough early schedule that includes the Pittsburgh Steelers, Jacksonville Jaguars, and Buffalo Bills?
